words.definitionEn: to offer to do something freely, without being required to

words.example: Organic produce is grown without pesticides, which some studies suggest may be harmful.

words.example: More families are trying to eat organic, but the cost remains a barrier for many.

words.example: Growing your own vegetables makes you feel closer to the source of what you eat.

words.definitionEn: standard modern agriculture using synthetic chemicals and intensive methods
words.example: Conventional farming produces higher yields but is often criticised for its environmental impact.

words.definitionEn: synthetic chemicals added to soil to increase crop growth

words.definitionEn: the practice of growing different crops on the same land in successive seasons

words.definitionEn: providing the body with essential nutrients needed for good health

words.definitionEn: the degree to which a food benefits one's physical wellbeing

words.definitionEn: to pull a root vegetable out of the ground; to harvest it

words.definitionEn: a method of farming that uses synthetic chemicals and intensive techniques

words.definitionEn: poisonous substances that are harmful to the body

words.definitionEn: to remove undesirable characteristics through selective breeding

words.definitionEn: methods and practices used in agriculture
words.example: New farming techniques are being developed to combine high yields with environmental sustainability.

words.definitionEn: data about the nutrients contained in a food product
